archetypes.name: The Rewrite Everything
archetypes.tagline: This could be so much better from scratch
archetypes.description: You're drawn to greenfield projects and reimagining systems. Legacy code feels like a puzzle you want to solve by replacing it. You see potential where others see constraints.
traits: Strong opinions on 'the right way' to build
strengths: Not afraid to challenge status quo
challenges: May rewrite things that didn't need rewriting
Risk of creating new legacy in pursuit of perfection

archetypes.name: The Ship It
archetypes.description: You have a bias for action and comfort with imperfection. Shipping features and learning from users matters more than architectural elegance. You keep teams moving forward.
challenges: May accumulate debt that slows future work

archetypes.name: The Detective
archetypes.tagline: I need to understand why first
archetypes.description: You're compelled to understand root causes before acting. Debugging is your element. You won't rest until you know exactly why something behaves the way it does.
traits: Digs deep into logs and stack traces
challenges: May delay shipping to satisfy curiosity

archetypes.name: The Craftsman
archetypes.description: You care deeply about readability, naming, structure, and elegance. Code is communication. You leave every file better than you found it.
traits: Strong opinions on style and naming
challenges: Can over-polish at the expense of speed

archetypes.name: The Calm Senior
archetypes.description: You're unflappable under pressure. You've learned when to act fast and when to slow down. Context and priorities guide you more than urgency.
challenges: May seem detached or slow to juniors

archetypes.name: The Experimenter
archetypes.tagline: Let's try it and see what happens
archetypes.description: You learn by doing. Prototypes, spikes, and experiments are how you think. You're comfortable breaking things in pursuit of understanding.
traits: Often works in branches and throwaway code
challenges: May undervalue planning and design phases

archetypes.name: The Glue Dev
archetypes.description: You unlock others by coordinating, clarifying, and connecting. You see gaps in communication and fill them. Teams run smoother when you're involved.
traits: Values team velocity over personal output
strengths: Often trusted as tech lead or liaison
challenges: May write less code than peers
Risk of burnout from context switching

archetypes.name: The Grow the Junior
archetypes.tagline: Let me show you how this works
archetypes.description: You're a patient teacher invested in team growth. You see potential in others and take time to explain reasoning, not just solutions.
strengths: Improves team culture and knowledge sharing
challenges: May be over-relied upon for help
Can be frustrated by lack of curiosity

archetypes.name: The Historian
archetypes.tagline: That was added after the 2019 outage
archetypes.description: You're the living memory of the codebase. You know why decisions were made, what was tried before, and which skeletons are in which closets.
traits: Often consulted for 'why does X exist?'
challenges: May resist change due to past failures
Can become a single point of failure

archetypes.name: The Architecture Astronaut
archetypes.tagline: How does this fit the bigger picture?
archetypes.description: You think in systems, patterns, and long-term design. You're drawn to abstractions and frameworks. You see how pieces should fit together.
traits: Drawn to design patterns and principles

archetypes.name: The AI-First Dev
archetypes.tagline: I'll ask AI to scaffold this
archetypes.description: You embrace AI tools, automation, and augmentation. You're comfortable offloading boilerplate and learning through generated code. You see AI as a teammate.
strengths: Efficient at boilerplate and repetitive tasks
challenges: May rely too much on generated patterns
Sometimes ships code they don't fully understand

archetypes.name: The Comfort Zone Keeper
archetypes.tagline: Let's stick with what we know works
archetypes.description: You prefer mastery over novelty. You value stability, proven tools, and deep expertise. You're skeptical of trends and prefer building on solid ground.
